Epsilon-constraint method for two objectives

Source: R/multiobjective.R
opt_epsilon_constraint.Rd

Traces a Pareto front by optimizing primary subject to secondary <= epsilon (for minimization; >= for maximization) over a grid of epsilon values. Unlike weighted sums, this reaches points on nonconvex parts of the front. Points can be weakly Pareto optimal; a second lexicographic stage would remove dominated ties.

Usage

opt_epsilon_constraint(model, primary, secondary, epsilon, ...)

Arguments

model

An opt_model().

primary, secondary

Scalar expressions.

epsilon

Numeric vector of bounds on secondary.

...

Further arguments for opt_solve().

Value

A data frame with epsilon, status, the two objective values, with the results in the results attribute.

Examples

m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", lower = 0, upper = 4)
y <- opt_variable(m, "y", lower = 0, upper = 4)
opt_constraint(m, x + y >= 4)
opt_epsilon_constraint(m, 2 * x + y, x + 3 * y, epsilon = c(4, 8, 12))
#>   epsilon  status primary secondary
#> 1       4 optimal       8         4
#> 2       8 optimal       6         8
#> 3      12 optimal       4        12
